To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
employees who volunteer for a nonprofit organization are perceived to be more committed, more helpful, and more cooperative than employees who do not volunteer.

employee volunteers were perceived to have higher performance ratings than non-volunteers, and that the relationship between volunteering and performance ratings was stronger for volunteers who had higher levels of volunteering than volunteers who had lower levels of volunteering.
employee volunteering is perceived as a positive activity that enhances the employee's credibility and is not perceived as a stigmatized activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how employee volunteering is perceived by colleagues.
the effects of volunteering on employee attitudes and behavior, and with the factors that influence these effects.
how employee volunteers are evaluated and treated by their colleagues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
employee volunteering is beneficial to both the organization and the employee.
employee volunteering is not only beneficial to the organization but also to the employees.
employee volunteering has a negative impact on employee commitment and performance, but only in some cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more we know about the employee, the more accurate our predictions about their performance will be.

we have demonstrated that the effects of employee volunteering on performance and commitment depend on whether employees perceive their colleagues to be supportive of their volunteering behavior or to be critical of it.
employee volunteering is a win-win situation for both the employee and the organization, as long as the employee perceives the activity as a valued contribution to the organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employee volunteering is not a one size fits all proposition.
employees should volunteer for causes that are meaningful to them, but they shouldn’t volunteer for causes that don’t align with their personal values.
employees who volunteer are more engaged and more productive.
